$schema_note: Points where 12 NYCRR 325-1.25, or a restatement of it, leaves a reading open. REGISTERED, NOT RESOLVED. Each names who would have to settle it. Entries tagged to a restatement version are that restatement's own ambiguity, not the regulation's.
$method_note: Nine registered from the regulation and the two layers read against each other. None gates an evaluation with a resolution key: the register encodes each text as it reads and lets the replay show where the readings part.

ambiguities.question: Does the carrier's 45-day clock start at receipt or at submission?

competing_readings.basis: (c)(1): `within 45 days after the bill has been received`.

(c)(3): `within 45 days of submission`; (d)(1): `no earlier than 45 days from the date of the submission`; (d)(4)(ii): `within 45 days after the bill was submitted`. Layer B says `submitted` throughout, and its quoted (c)(1) says `submitted` where the compilation says `received`.

ambiguities.materiality: Every timeliness determination in (c) and (d) turns on which day is day zero; a bill received days after submission moves the deadline by that many days.
ambiguities.who_settles: The Board, by amendment or on a disputed bill.

ambiguities.question: Are the section's `days` (120, 45, 30) calendar days or business days?

competing_readings.basis: No qualifier; the (b)(1) example `120 days from January 1, 2020 (April 30, 2020)` is 120 calendar days.
Nothing in the text excludes it.

ambiguities.materiality: Every interval clause. The register uses calendar_days, on the strength of the (b)(1) example, and marks it as an assumption.

ambiguities.question: What is payment `in full`: the full amount billed, or the full amount up to the fee schedule maximum?

competing_readings.basis: (c)(3): `the full amount billed`; (d)(1): `not been paid in full or in part`.
(c)(3) continues `up to the maximum amount established in the applicable fee schedule`; (d)(6): an award `not in excess of the fee schedule`.

ambiguities.textual_basis: (c)(3), (d)(1), (d)(6); layer A `has not paid your bill in full`; layer B `pay the bill in full up to the maximum`.
ambiguities.materiality: Whether a carrier that paid the schedule amount on a bill above it has paid `in full` decides the (d)(1) remedy under layer A's reading.
ambiguities.who_settles: The Board; the maximum itself sits in the licensed schedule (stated_elsewhere_purchase_required).
ambiguities.$anchored_on: (d)(1), which the regulation and layer A both carry; the same phrase in (c)(3) and in layer B's restatement of it is the same question and is noted in textual_basis rather than anchored twice.

ambiguities.question: `have not been paid in full or in part`: not paid in full (partial payment counts as unpaid), or not paid at all in any part?

competing_readings.basis: `in full or in part` qualifies `paid`: a partial payment leaves the bill not paid in full.
The phrase could mean no payment was made, in full or in part.

ambiguities.materiality: Whether a partially paid bill can go to an administrative award or only to arbitration.

ambiguities.question: (g) says the regulation is effective 2020-01-01; the compilation records amendments effective 2020-01-29 and 2021-11-01. Which text was in force on a given date?

competing_readings.reading: (g) dates the 2020 text; the amendments date themselves
(g) is stale and was not updated
competing_readings.basis: (g) was not amended when the section was.

ambiguities.materiality: Which version of (c)(1) governs a 2020 or 2021 bill; layer B quotes a text that is not the current one.
ambiguities.who_settles: The Department of State's compilation (not retrieved) and the Board.

ambiguities.question: Layer A says the provider `may be able to` request the Board's assistance. Is that a statement of the remedy's condition or a hedge that leaves the condition unstated?

competing_readings.reading: The stated condition is the condition
competing_readings.basis: The sentence gives one condition, non-payment in full within 45 days.
`may be able to` concedes other conditions exist without naming them.

ambiguities.textual_basis: Layer A hub page, `Medical billing issues/disputes`.
ambiguities.materiality: The pay-or-object hypothesis: the register encodes the stated condition and records the hedge here.
ambiguities.who_settles: The Board, as author of the page.

ambiguities.question: Layer B requires legal and MTG objections `on Form C-81.B`. No Board form carries that identifier; the Board's legal-objection form is C-8.1B. Typo, or a form this session did not find?

competing_readings.basis: One transposed character; the same article names C-8.4 correctly.
This session did not retrieve the Board's form index.

ambiguities.materiality: Encoded literally, every legal and MTG objection is nonconforming under layer B. The divergence on those clauses is the typo's.
ambiguities.who_settles: daisyBill, as author; the Board's form index would show whether C-81.B exists.

ambiguities.question: `has not objected in the manner described herein`: does the manner include the prescribed format, so that a timely objection in the wrong format leaves the carrier liable in full?

competing_readings.basis: `in the manner described herein` points at (c)(1), which prescribes the format.
(c)(3) is headed by the 45-day figure and the Board's own restatement (layer B) reads it as timing.

ambiguities.materiality: The register's (c)(3) tests timing and kinds only and does not consume the format meaning: a stated limit chosen because a clause rests on one ungrounded term.

ambiguities.question: When is a legal or MTG issue `finally determined adversely` to the carrier, given that (f)(3) lets a section 23 review stay payment and then says further appeals do not?

competing_readings.reading: At the judge's or Panel decision
competing_readings.basis: (f)(3) names those decisions as the ones that end withholding.

competing_readings.reading: At the exhaustion of all appeals

ambiguities.materiality: When the 30-day count to an award or arbitration request begins.
